Weekly Signal — August 17–23, 2026

4 new archive items, 3 active builds, and a clean-room rebuild of LUMON MDR / Severance Refiner.

New in the archive

The latest publication date gathers 4 articles.

  • The Trail You Leave Is the Story
    Think about the last time you tried to figure out what happened at work last month. Not what the report says happened — what actually happened. Who was waiting on whom. Which thing sat untouched for weeks. When the deal really went quiet, as opposed to when someone finally wrote "lost" in the system.
  • The Negative
    Someone asks what happened with an account. You open the system. Status: In Progress. Owner assigned, last updated a couple of weeks ago, nothing overdue. By everything the record says, it is fine.
  • The Colony Calls the Twin
    Every quarter hour a watchdog on my desk writes one line: a frame. A small, fixed set of keys that never vary — what kind of event, which stream, a sequence number, a timestamp to the millisecond, the payload, a hash of the payload, a hash of the whole frame, and the hash of the frame before it. Two neighbors do the same, on their own streams, and each can r
  • Scrape Yourself
    In 2020 Simon Willison gave a name to something he had been doing since a hurricane in 2017: point a GitHub Actions cron at a URL, fetch it, commit the file if it changed, and let git keep the history. He called it git scraping. His line for why it works is the one worth remembering: the changes in a data source "can sometimes be more interesting than the un

Active builds

  • rapp-roadmap — 🗺️ The RAPP roadmap: one laptop brainstem -> a planetary swarm of governed Leviathans enhancing every Agent 365 workflow. Enhance, never replace; kernel stays sacred.
  • rapp-spine — 🦴 Crawl the spine — a situational router over the full RAPP protocol stack. Situation -> layer -> protocol, collisions named.
  • RAPP-Bible — One repo. Every RAPP spec. Every entry point. Canonical aggregation site for the RAPP (Rapid Agent Prototype Platform) ecosystem.

Rediscovered

Ledger Grammars: Turning Narrative Frames Into Queryable State — Once a system starts thinking in frames, the next problem appears immediately.

Lost App → clean-room lesson

LUMON MDR / Severance Refiner: A mysterious retro-corporate number game rebuilt as an original deterministic state-machine challenge.

Open the rebuild lesson · Run the local demo

RAPP Vision brief

The strangest lost app asks you to identify numbers that simply feel wrong.

Reverse-engineering a mysterious selection mechanic into a deterministic state-machine game.

Short: Which of these numbers looks wrong?
